## Dscam1: diversity by combination {#sec-dscam}

Drosophila *Dscam1* is the clearest demonstration in any organism that a single
gene can specify an enormous protein repertoire through splicing alone, and that
the repertoire size is itself under selection.

![Three mutually exclusive exon clusters and one alternative transmembrane exon
generate the *Dscam1* repertoire. A single neuron uses a small, probabilistically
drawn slice of it.](../figures/dscam-combinatorics.svg){#fig-dscam width=100%}

_Scope:_ the combinatorial architecture and the arithmetic; homophilic binding
specificity and self-avoidance; how many isoforms one neuron actually uses; the
cis RNA-structure mechanism that enforces mutual exclusivity; the CRISPR
deletion series separating a saturating requirement for dendrite self/non-self
discrimination from a cluster-identity-dependent requirement for axon
patterning; and the evidence that isoform *bias*, not only isoform *number*, is
functional.

## Other landmark cases

_Scope:_ sex determination (*Sxl*/*tra*/*dsx*) as a splicing switch controlling a
developmental decision; CD45/*PTPRC* in lymphocyte activation; *BCL2L1* and other
opposing-function isoform pairs; titin and tissue mechanics; *FGFR2* IIIb/IIIc;
PKM1/PKM2, recorded with the conflict between the splice-forcing phenotype and
the absolute quantification that finds PKM2 already predominant in several normal
tissues.

## How much of this is functional

_Scope:_ the genome-wide prevalence numbers and, more importantly, their
inclusion rules. The widely repeated "95% of multi-exon genes" figure means
different things at different abundance thresholds and over different
denominators, and the chapter states them rather than picking one.
